criterion: At a phone width each finding in a chapter keeps its heading and prose directly above its own chart as one unit.
evaluation_rule: A chapter is one of the three long report pages, such as 01 Tools; a finding is a numbered heading with prose and a chart. Open 01 Tools at a phone width and scroll through all three findings. Yes if every finding shows its heading and prose immediately above its own chart, with nothing else placed between a claim and its chart. No if a heading or its prose ends up on a different stretch of the page from its chart, or if the chart comes before its claim.

criterion: The cover's title block stays legible at every moment as the gradient ground drifts behind the title.
evaluation_rule: The cover is the report's front page at the root address, with the title Studio Signals in a solid block over a drifting coloured ground. Watch the title for twenty seconds while the ground moves. Yes if the title reads clearly the whole time because a solid dark block sits behind the lettering. No if the title ever becomes hard to read as brighter or darker parts of the ground pass behind it.

criterion: On a chapter, a chart that has already grown into view stays still when the reader scrolls away and back to the chart.
evaluation_rule: A chart is the bar drawing beside a finding on a chapter page such as 01 Tools. Scroll a chart into view and let its bars finish growing, scroll well past it, then scroll back up to it. Yes if on the return the bars are already at full length and do not grow again. No if the bars shrink and regrow every time the chart re-enters the window.

criterion: When a chapter chart first enters view its bars grow out in a cascade from the top bar downwards.
evaluation_rule: A chart is the bar drawing beside a finding on a chapter page; the What is in the stack chart on 01 Tools has five bars. Load 01 Tools and scroll slowly until that chart first enters the window. Yes if the bars grow from zero to their lengths one after another, each starting a moment after the one above, the whole cascade finishing in about a second. No if every bar appears at once at full length, or if the bars grow all together with no cascade.

criterion: At a phone width a chapter keeps its section list one tap away, with the current section still marked.
evaluation_rule: The rail is the list of a chapter's findings and closers shown down the left at a wide window. Open 02 Craft at a phone width, scroll to the second finding, then open the Sections control. Yes if a sheet lists every finding and closer with Confidence by company size marked as the current section, and choosing an entry jumps there and closes the sheet. No if the section list is unreachable at the phone width, or if the sheet marks no current section.

criterion: The part-to-whole chart on a chapter still separates its options when the page is viewed in greyscale.
evaluation_rule: The part-to-whole chart is the single full-width bar split into option segments beside How often designers use AI on 01 Tools. View that chart with the browser's greyscale rendering or a greyscale screenshot. Yes if each of the five segments remains distinguishable from its neighbours and matchable to its key entry. No if two neighbouring segments merge into one indistinguishable grey block.

criterion: Moving from one chapter to the next keeps the reader's chosen segment in force on the new chapter.
evaluation_rule: A chapter is one of the three report pages; the segment is the company size, work environment or experience group chosen in the sidebar. On 01 Tools choose Enterprise (2,000+), then use the next-chapter control at the foot of the chapter. Yes if 02 Craft opens already showing Enterprise (2,000+) in its state line with its figures for that group. No if the new chapter opens showing all respondents, forcing the group to be chosen again.

criterion: The citation panel beneath a chapter chart offers the citation as a sentence, a structured record and a bare address, each easy to copy on its own.
evaluation_rule: The citation panel opens from Cite this finding beneath any chart on a chapter page. Open it for the first finding of 01 Tools. Yes if the panel presents three separate shapes of the same citation, a readable sentence, a structured record and the address, each selectable without dragging across the others. No if only one shape is offered, or if the three run together so one cannot be taken without the rest.

criterion: On a very wide window the body prose of a chapter stays in a comfortable reading column.
evaluation_rule: Body prose is the paragraphs under each finding heading on a chapter page such as 03 Teams. Open 03 Teams on the widest window available and read a paragraph. Yes if each line of prose stays short enough to follow back to the next line comfortably, with the column not stretching across the whole window. No if prose lines run most of the window's width, making the next line hard to find.

criterion: Under a segment too small to report, a chapter's withdrawn findings read as deliberate explanations rather than broken charts.
evaluation_rule: A withdrawn finding is what a chapter shows in place of a chart when the chosen group has too few respondents. Open 02 Craft filtered to Growth (51 to 500) with Freelance. Yes if each finding keeps a composed layout with its title and a clear explanation in place of the chart, consistent across all three findings. No if the chart areas look empty, collapsed, zero-length or broken.

criterion: On a chapter, a link in the prose changes its colour and its underline together as one smooth movement on hover.
evaluation_rule: A prose link is an underlined link inside a chapter's paragraphs, such as the methodology link after a source line. Move the pointer onto and off such a link several times. Yes if the text colour and the underline change together in one smooth movement each way. No if the change snaps instantly, or if the colour and the underline change at different moments.

criterion: Tabbing through a chapter's sidebar shows which link or control holds focus at every step.
evaluation_rule: The sidebar is the left column of a chapter page holding the destinations, the chapter links, the segment selects and the rail. On 01 Tools press Tab from the top of the page through every sidebar item. Yes if at each step a clearly visible outline marks the focused item. No if focus moves through any item with no visible mark.

criterion: At a phone width a chapter chart with long option labels stays readable at a glance, each label matched to its bar.
evaluation_rule: A chart is the bar drawing beside a finding; What makes a tool stick and What is in the stack have several labelled options. Open 01 Tools at a phone width and look at the What is in the stack chart. Yes if every label can be read in full and matched to its own bar at a glance, with the bars still long enough to compare. No if labels are cut off, overlap one another, or crowd the bars until the lengths can no longer be compared.
